category: Selection, Image, Edit and Type operations
description: The Select, Image, Edit and Type menus: making and refining selections, changing document mode, size, canvas and orientation, the clipboard, fill, stroke, transform and warp commands, preset and preference management, and the typography panels and conversion commands. Shortcuts are the Windows defaults.

tools.name: Select > All
tools.description: Selects the entire canvas of the active layer or document. Used before a copy, a fill, a stroke around the whole frame, or a transform that must include everything, and as the starting point for a subtractive selection.
tools.usage: Select > All (Ctrl+A).
tools.example:
1. Ctrl+A to select the whole canvas.
2. Edit > Stroke..., 8 px, Inside, black, to draw a border.
3. Ctrl+D to deselect.

JSX: app.activeDocument.selection.selectAll();

tools.name: Select > Deselect
tools.description: Clears the active selection so that subsequent edits apply to the whole layer again. Forgetting to deselect is the single most common reason a filter, brush or adjustment appears to do nothing outside a hidden selection.
tools.usage: Select > Deselect (Ctrl+D).
tools.example:
Ctrl+D after any masked edit.

JSX: app.activeDocument.selection.deselect();
tools.notes: Ctrl+H hides the selection edges without deselecting - useful while judging an edit, but easy to forget.

tools.name: Select > Reselect
tools.description: Restores the last selection that was deselected, as long as no new selection has been made since. A quick undo for an accidental Ctrl+D without stepping back through the History panel.
tools.usage: Select > Reselect (Shift+Ctrl+D).
tools.example:
1. Spend a minute building a careful selection.
2. Press Ctrl+D by accident.
3. Shift+Ctrl+D to get it back.
tools.notes: For a selection you will need again later, store it as an alpha channel with Select > Save Selection instead.

tools.name: Select > Inverse
tools.description: Swaps the selected and unselected areas. The standard second step after selecting a subject or a plain background: select whichever is easier, then invert.
tools.usage: Select > Inverse (Shift+Ctrl+I).
tools.example:
1. Magic Wand the white background of a product shot.
2. Shift+Ctrl+I so the product is selected.
3. Click Add Layer Mask.

JSX: app.activeDocument.selection.invert();

tools.name: Select > All Layers and layer selection commands
tools.description: Layer-level selection rather than pixel selection: All Layers selects every layer except the Background, Deselect Layers clears the layer selection, Find Layers opens the Layers panel filter, and Isolate Layers shows only the selected layers by switching the panel filter to Selected. Useful before grouping, aligning or bulk-restyling.
tools.usage: Select > All Layers (Alt+Ctrl+A), Select > Deselect Layers, Select > Find Layers (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+F), Select > Isolate Layers.
tools.example:
1. Alt+Ctrl+A to select every layer.
2. Ctrl+G to put them all in one group.
3. Select > Isolate Layers while working on a subset, then switch the Layers panel filter off to see everything again.

tools.name: Select > Color Range
tools.description: Builds a selection from sampled colours or from predefined ranges, with a Fuzziness slider that controls how far the match spreads and a live greyscale preview of the resulting mask. Beyond sampled colours it offers Reds/Yellows/Greens/Cyans/Blues/Magentas, Highlights/Midtones/Shadows, Out of Gamut and Skin Tones with a Detect Faces option - the most controllable way to select by tone or colour.
tools.usage: Select > Color Range...

parameters.name: Select
parameters.description: Sampled Colors, a named colour family, Highlights/Midtones/Shadows, Skin Tones, Out of Gamut.

parameters.name: Fuzziness
parameters.description: 0-200; widens or tightens the tolerance around the sampled colour.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Available for Highlights/Midtones/Shadows - which slice of the tonal range counts.

parameters.name: Localized Color Clusters
parameters.description: Keeps the selection near where you sampled instead of matching the same colour everywhere.

parameters.name: Eyedroppers
parameters.description: Sample, add to sample (Shift) and subtract from sample (Alt).

parameters.name: Invert / Selection Preview
parameters.description: Flip the mask; preview it on the canvas as None, Grayscale, Black Matte, White Matte or Quick Mask.

tools.example:
1. Select > Color Range, Select = Skin Tones, tick Detect Faces.
2. Set Fuzziness to about 40 and watch the preview.
3. OK, then add a Hue/Saturation adjustment layer - the selection becomes its mask.

tools.name: Select > Focus Area
tools.description: Selects the in-focus parts of an image by analysing local sharpness, which separates a subject from a shallow-depth-of-field background without tracing its outline. In-Focus Range controls the threshold, Image Noise Level handles grainy files, and the result can be handed straight to Select and Mask for edge refinement.
tools.usage: Select > Focus Area...

parameters.name: In-Focus Range
parameters.description: 0-10; higher values include softer areas in the selection.

parameters.name: Image Noise Level
parameters.description: Advanced setting that stops noise being read as detail.

parameters.name: Add / Subtract tools
parameters.description: Brush over areas the analysis got wrong.

parameters.name: Output To
parameters.description: Selection, Layer Mask, New Layer, New Layer with Layer Mask, New Document.

tools.example:
1. Open a portrait shot at f/1.8.
2. Select > Focus Area, let the auto analysis settle, then nudge In-Focus Range until the hair is included.
3. Click Select and Mask... to refine the edges, Output To = Layer Mask.
tools.notes: Needs the graphics processor enabled and works poorly on evenly sharp images such as flat scans.

tools.name: Select > Subject
tools.description: Adobe Sensei one-click selection of the most prominent subject or subjects in the image. It is the usual starting point for a cut-out: run it, then refine in Select and Mask or with the Quick Selection tool. Newer releases offer a cloud-processed option that is slower but more accurate on hair and fine detail.
tools.usage: Select > Subject, the Select Subject button in the options bar of the Object Selection, Quick Selection and Magic Wand tools, or the Contextual Task Bar.
tools.example:
1. Select > Subject.
2. Shift-drag with the Quick Selection tool to add anything it missed.
3. Click the Add Layer Mask button to cut the subject out non-destructively.
tools.notes: Select > Sky is the complementary command for landscapes, and the Object Selection tool selects one chosen object rather than the whole subject.

tools.name: Select > Sky
tools.description: Automatically selects the sky, handling the soft transitions through foliage and building edges that manual selection struggles with. Used for darkening or replacing a sky, and as the selection behind Edit > Sky Replacement, which performs the whole swap including colour harmonisation.
tools.usage: Select > Sky. The full replacement workflow is Edit > Sky Replacement...
tools.example:
1. Select > Sky.
2. Add a Curves adjustment layer - the sky selection becomes its mask.
3. Pull the curve down to deepen the sky only.

Or run Edit > Sky Replacement... to swap in a different sky with automatic foreground colour matching.

tools.name: Select and Mask workspace
tools.description: The dedicated refinement workspace for any selection or mask. It provides the Quick Selection, Refine Edge Brush, Brush, Object Selection, Lasso and Polygon Lasso tools alongside Radius, Smooth, Feather, Contrast and Shift Edge sliders, Decontaminate Colors to remove background fringing, and several preview modes (Onion Skin, Marching Ants, Overlay, On Black, On White, Black & White, On Layers). The Refine Edge Brush is what makes hair and fur selections possible.
tools.usage: Select > Select and Mask... (Alt+Ctrl+R), or the Select and Mask button in a selection tool's options bar, or Properties panel > Select and Mask with a mask active.

parameters.name: Radius / Smart Radius
parameters.description: Width of the band around the edge that Photoshop re-analyses; Smart Radius adapts it to the edge type.

parameters.name: Smooth / Feather / Contrast / Shift Edge
parameters.description: Global edge shaping: simplify the outline, soften it, harden it, and expand or contract it.

parameters.name: Decontaminate Colors
parameters.description: Replaces fringe colour picked up from the old background; forces a new layer output.

parameters.name: Output To
parameters.description: Selection, Layer Mask, New Layer, New Layer with Layer Mask, New Document, New Document with Layer Mask.

tools.example:
1. Select > Subject, then Alt+Ctrl+R.
2. View = On Black, Radius 3 px, tick Smart Radius.
3. Paint the hairline with the Refine Edge Brush.
4. Shift Edge -8%, tick Decontaminate Colors, Output To = New Layer with Layer Mask.

tools.name: Select > Modify (Border, Smooth, Expand, Contract, Feather)
tools.description: Five geometric operations on an existing selection. They are the quick, numeric way to fix a selection that is slightly too tight, too ragged or too hard-edged, without returning to the selection tool.
tools.usage: Select > Modify > Border... / Smooth... / Expand... / Contract... / Feather... (Feather is also Shift+F6).

parameters.name: Border
parameters.description: 1-200 px; replaces the selection with a soft-edged band of that width straddling the original edge.

parameters.name: Smooth
parameters.description: 1-100 px sample radius; rounds off corners and removes stray single-pixel islands.

parameters.name: Expand
parameters.description: 1-100 px; grows the selection outwards uniformly.

parameters.name: Contract
parameters.description: 1-100 px; shrinks it inwards - used to pull a selection just inside an edge before filling.

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.description: 0.1-1000 px; softens the edge so the change blends. Apply at the resolution you are working at.

tools.example:
Removing a halo after a cut-out:
1. Ctrl+click the mask thumbnail to load it as a selection.
2. Select > Modify > Contract, 2 px.
3. Select > Modify > Feather, 0.5 px.
4. Fill the mask with the modified selection.

JSX: var s = app.activeDocument.selection; s.contract(2); s.feather(0.5);

tools.name: Select > Grow and Select > Similar
tools.description: Extend a selection by colour using the Magic Wand's current Tolerance setting. Grow adds adjacent pixels within tolerance, spreading the selection outwards from where it already is; Similar adds every matching pixel anywhere in the layer, however far away. Repeated application keeps extending.
tools.usage: Select > Grow, Select > Similar. Both read the Tolerance value in the Magic Wand tool's options bar.
tools.example:
1. Magic Wand one blue button in a screenshot.
2. Select > Similar - every button of that blue is now selected.
3. Add a Hue/Saturation layer to recolour them all at once.
tools.notes: Set the Magic Wand tolerance before running the command; there is no dialog to set it afterwards.

tools.name: Save Selection, Load Selection and Transform Selection
tools.description: Persistence and adjustment for selections. Save Selection stores the selection as an alpha channel in the document (or as a layer mask), Load Selection brings it back with Boolean options against the current selection, and Transform Selection scales, rotates, skews and warps the selection outline itself without touching any pixels.
tools.usage: Select > Save Selection... / Load Selection... / Transform Selection. Ctrl+click a channel, mask or layer thumbnail also loads it as a selection (add Shift to union, Alt to subtract, Shift+Alt to intersect).

parameters.name: Save Selection: Document / Channel
parameters.description: Target document and either a new channel or an existing one, with Replace, Add, Subtract and Intersect operations.

parameters.name: Load Selection: Invert
parameters.description: Loads the inverse of the stored channel.

parameters.name: Transform Selection
parameters.description: Shows the free-transform box around the marching ants; Enter commits, Esc cancels.

tools.name: Image > Mode
tools.description: Converts the document's colour model and bit depth. Mode changes are lossy in one direction - RGB to CMYK discards out-of-gamut colours, 16-bit to 8-bit discards tonal precision, colour to Grayscale discards hue - so convert as late as possible and keep the master in the widest mode. Some filters and features are only available in 8-bit RGB.
tools.usage: Image > Mode > Bitmap / Grayscale / Duotone / Indexed Color / RGB Color / CMYK Color / Lab Color / Multichannel, and Image > Mode > 8 Bits/Channel / 16 Bits/Channel / 32 Bits/Channel.

parameters.name: RGB Color
parameters.description: The working mode for screen, web and almost all editing; required by many filters.

parameters.name: CMYK Color
parameters.description: Four-ink print separation. Convert at the end, using the correct output profile in Edit > Color Settings.

parameters.name: Grayscale
parameters.description: Single channel. Use the Black & White adjustment first to control how hues map to grey.

parameters.name: Lab Color
parameters.description: Lightness plus two colour axes - useful for sharpening or colour work that must not shift luminance.

parameters.name: Indexed Color
parameters.description: Up to 256 colours with a palette, dither and transparency options; for GIF and legacy formats.

parameters.name: Bitmap
parameters.description: Pure 1-bit black and white (requires Grayscale first), with 50% Threshold, Pattern Dither, Diffusion Dither and Halftone Screen methods.

parameters.name: Duotone
parameters.description: Monotone, duotone, tritone and quadtone ink curves for rich single- and two-colour printing (requires Grayscale first).

parameters.name: 8 / 16 / 32 Bits/Channel
parameters.description: Tonal precision. 16-bit for heavy tonal editing and raw files, 32-bit for HDR.

tools.notes: Ctrl+Y (View > Proof Colors) soft-proofs a CMYK conversion without actually converting the file.

tools.name: Image > Image Size
tools.description: Changes the pixel dimensions, the print size and the resolution of the document. With Resample off it only redistributes the existing pixels across a different physical size; with Resample on Photoshop adds or removes pixels using the chosen interpolation method. Preserve Details 2.0 is the best upscaler in the dialog, and Bicubic Sharper the standard choice for reduction.
tools.usage: Image > Image Size... (Alt+Ctrl+I).

parameters.name: Width / Height / Units
parameters.description: Pixels, percent, inches, cm, mm, points, picas. The chain icon constrains the aspect ratio.

parameters.name: Resolution
parameters.description: Pixels per inch or per cm; only meaningful for print output.

parameters.name: Resample
parameters.description: Off preserves the pixel count. On enables the interpolation menu.

parameters.name: Interpolation
parameters.description: Automatic, Preserve Details / Preserve Details 2.0 (enlargement), Bicubic Smoother, Bicubic Sharper (reduction), Bicubic, Nearest Neighbor (hard edges, pixel art), Bilinear.

parameters.name: Fit To
parameters.description: Preset target sizes and saved custom presets.

tools.name: Image > Canvas Size
tools.description: Changes the size of the canvas without scaling the image on it, adding empty space or cropping from the chosen anchor. Used to add a border or a caption strip, to pad an image to a required aspect ratio, and to trim edges numerically.
tools.usage: Image > Canvas Size... (Alt+Ctrl+C).

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: New canvas dimensions in the chosen units.

parameters.name: Relative
parameters.description: Treats the values as an amount to add (or, if negative, remove) rather than an absolute size.

parameters.name: Anchor
parameters.description: Nine-position grid deciding where the existing image sits in the new canvas.

parameters.name: Canvas extension color
parameters.description: Foreground, Background, White, Black, Grey or Other. Transparent when the layer is not a Background.

tools.example:
Add an even 100 px white border:
1. Alt+Ctrl+C, tick Relative.
2. Width 200 px, Height 200 px, Anchor centre, extension colour White.

JSX: app.activeDocument.resizeCanvas(UnitValue(2200,'px'), UnitValue(2200,'px'), AnchorPosition.MIDDLECENTER);

tools.name: Image > Image Rotation
tools.description: Rotates or flips the whole document, every layer together, by 180 degrees, 90 degrees clockwise or counter-clockwise, by an arbitrary angle, or mirrored horizontally or vertically. Distinct from Edit > Transform, which affects only the selected layers.
tools.usage: Image > Image Rotation > 180 degrees / 90 degrees Clockwise / 90 degrees Counter Clockwise / Arbitrary... / Flip Canvas Horizontal / Flip Canvas Vertical.
tools.notes: Flipping the canvas horizontally is a classic proofing trick - composition and drawing errors become obvious in mirror image.

tools.name: Image > Crop
tools.description: Crops the document to the current rectangular selection, discarding everything outside it on every layer. The keyboard-free alternative to the Crop tool when you already have a precise selection, and the command an action records for a fixed numeric crop.
tools.usage: Image > Crop (requires an active selection; a non-rectangular selection is cropped to its bounding box).
tools.example:
1. Rectangular Marquee with Style = Fixed Size, 1080 x 1080 px.
2. Click to place it, drag to position.
3. Image > Crop.

JSX: app.activeDocument.crop([100, 100, 1180, 1180]);

tools.name: Image > Trim
tools.description: Removes uniform borders automatically, based either on transparency or on the colour of the top-left or bottom-right pixel, with per-side control. The standard way to tighten a rendered asset down to its content and a staple of export actions.
tools.usage: Image > Trim...

parameters.name: Based On
parameters.description: Transparent Pixels, Top Left Pixel Color, Bottom Right Pixel Color.

parameters.name: Trim Away
parameters.description: Top, Bottom, Left, Right checkboxes.

tools.name: Image > Reveal All
tools.description: Expands the canvas until every pixel of every layer is inside it, revealing content that was pushed outside the visible area by moving or pasting. The fastest way to recover artwork you can no longer see, and the natural counterpart of Trim.
tools.usage: Image > Reveal All.
tools.example:
1. A pasted layer sits mostly off-canvas.
2. Image > Reveal All - the canvas grows to contain it.
3. Reposition, then crop back to the size you want.

tools.name: Image > Duplicate
tools.description: Creates a copy of the current document in memory, optionally flattened ("Duplicate Merged Layers Only"), without touching the file on disk. Used before a destructive step such as Flatten, a mode conversion or HDR Toning, and inside scripts that need a throwaway working copy.
tools.usage: Image > Duplicate...

parameters.name: As
parameters.description: Name of the duplicate document.

parameters.name: Duplicate Merged Layers Only
parameters.description: Produces a single flattened layer instead of the full layer stack.

tools.name: Image > Apply Image
tools.description: Blends a source layer or channel - from this document or another open document of the same pixel dimensions - into the active layer or channel using any blend mode, opacity, optional mask and optional inversion. The engine behind frequency separation, luminosity masks and channel-based sharpening.
tools.usage: Image > Apply Image...

parameters.name: Source / Layer / Channel
parameters.description: Which document, which layer (or Merged) and which channel (RGB, R, G, B, an alpha channel, or Transparency) supplies the data.

parameters.name: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the source before blending.

parameters.name: Blending / Opacity
parameters.description: Any blend mode plus Add and Subtract, which expose Scale and Offset.

parameters.name: Scale / Offset
parameters.description: Only for Add and Subtract: divide the result and shift it, e.g. Scale 2, Offset 128 for frequency separation.

parameters.name: Preserve Transparency / Mask
parameters.description: Protect transparent areas; restrict the blend through a channel or layer mask.

tools.example:
Frequency separation, high-frequency layer (8-bit):
1. Duplicate the layer twice; blur the lower copy (Gaussian Blur 6 px).
2. Select the top copy, Image > Apply Image: Layer = the blurred layer, Blending = Subtract, Scale 2, Offset 128.
3. Set the top layer's blend mode to Linear Light.

tools.name: Image > Calculations
tools.description: Blends two individual channels (from one or two documents of equal size) and writes the result to a new channel, a new document or a selection. The classic way to build a contrast-based mask - for example blending the blue channel with an inverted red channel to isolate a sky or a subject.
tools.usage: Image > Calculations...

parameters.name: Source 1 / Source 2
parameters.description: Document, layer and channel for each input, each with its own Invert checkbox.

parameters.name: Blending / Opacity / Mask
parameters.description: Blend mode combining the two channels, strength, and an optional masking channel.

parameters.name: Result
parameters.description: New Channel, New Document or Selection.

tools.example:
1. Image > Calculations.
2. Source 1 = Blue channel; Source 2 = Red channel with Invert ticked; Blending = Multiply.
3. Result = New Channel - an alpha channel that isolates the sky.
4. Ctrl+click the new channel to load it as a selection.

tools.name: Edit > Undo, Redo and Toggle Last State
tools.description: Photoshop's history navigation. Since the 2019 release Ctrl+Z steps backwards repeatedly through the History panel and Shift+Ctrl+Z steps forwards, while Alt+Ctrl+Z toggles between the last two states for a quick before/after comparison. The History panel itself gives random access to states and snapshots.
tools.usage: Edit > Undo (Ctrl+Z), Edit > Redo (Shift+Ctrl+Z), Edit > Toggle Last State (Alt+Ctrl+Z). Legacy CS-style shortcuts can be restored in Preferences > General.

parameters.name: History States
parameters.description: Preferences > Performance sets how many states are retained (default 50).

parameters.name: Snapshots
parameters.description: History panel > New Snapshot preserves a state beyond the rolling limit for the session.

tools.example:
1. Apply a strong grade.
2. Press Alt+Ctrl+Z repeatedly to flip between before and after.
3. For an older state, click it directly in Window > History.

tools.name: Edit > Fade
tools.description: Retroactively reduces the opacity of, or changes the blend mode of, the filter, adjustment or brush stroke you have just applied - but only if it is still the most recent operation. A fast way to dial an over-strong filter back, and to apply a filter in Luminosity mode so it does not shift colour.
tools.usage: Edit > Fade... (Shift+Ctrl+F), immediately after the operation.

parameters.name: Opacity
parameters.description: 0-100% of the applied effect.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Any blend mode - Luminosity after sharpening avoids colour fringing.

tools.example:
1. Filter > Sharpen > Unsharp Mask, Amount 150%.
2. Shift+Ctrl+F immediately, Opacity 60%, Mode = Luminosity.
tools.notes: Any other action in between disables the command. Smart Filters offer the same control permanently and are the better habit.

tools.name: Cut, Copy, Copy Merged and Paste commands
tools.description: The clipboard family. Copy takes the selection from the active layer, Copy Merged takes the composite of all visible layers, and the Paste Special submenu offers Paste in Place (same coordinates), Paste Into (pasted content becomes clipped to the selection with an automatic mask) and Paste Outside (clipped to everything except the selection).
tools.usage: Edit > Cut (Ctrl+X), Copy (Ctrl+C), Copy Merged (Shift+Ctrl+C), Paste (Ctrl+V), Paste Special > Paste in Place (Shift+Ctrl+V) / Paste Into (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+V) / Paste Outside.
tools.example:
Putting a photo inside a picture frame:
1. Select the inside of the frame with the Polygonal Lasso.
2. Copy the photo from another document (Ctrl+C).
3. Back in the frame document, Edit > Paste Special > Paste Into - the photo is masked to the frame opening and can be moved inside it.
tools.notes: Preferences > General > Export Clipboard controls whether the clipboard survives leaving Photoshop, which matters for large selections.

tools.name: Edit > Fill
tools.description: Fills the selection or layer with a colour, a pattern, History, or Content-Aware content. Content-Aware Fill opens a dedicated workspace with a green sampling-area overlay, rotation, scale and mirror adaptation, and a live preview - the main tool for removing objects from complex backgrounds alongside the Remove tool.
tools.usage: Edit > Fill... (Shift+F5). Alt+Backspace fills with the foreground colour, Ctrl+Backspace with the background colour. Edit > Content-Aware Fill... opens the workspace.

parameters.name: Contents
parameters.description: Foreground Color, Background Color, Color..., Content-Aware, Pattern, History, Black, 50% Gray, White.

parameters.name: Blending Mode / Opacity
parameters.description: How the fill composites with the existing pixels.

parameters.name: Preserve Transparency
parameters.description: Fills only pixels that are already opaque.

parameters.name: Content-Aware workspace
parameters.description: Sampling Area Overlay, Sampling Area Options (Auto/Rectangular/Custom), Color Adaptation, Rotation Adaptation, Scale, Mirror, Output To.

tools.example:
1. Lasso loosely around an unwanted sign, including a little background.
2. Edit > Content-Aware Fill...
3. Subtract the sky from the green sampling overlay with the brush, set Color Adaptation to High, Output To = New Layer, OK.

JSX: app.activeDocument.selection.fill(app.foregroundColor, ColorBlendMode.NORMAL, 100, false);

tools.name: Edit > Stroke
tools.description: Paints a line of a given width and colour along the edge of the selection or the layer's opaque pixels, positioned inside, centred or outside. Unlike the Stroke layer effect this writes real pixels, which is what you want when the result must be rasterised or edited with the brush.
tools.usage: Edit > Stroke... (with an active selection or a layer with transparency).

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Stroke thickness in pixels (or the current ruler unit).

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: Any colour from the picker.

parameters.name: Location
parameters.description: Inside, Center or Outside the selection edge.

parameters.name: Blending Mode / Opacity / Preserve Transparency
parameters.description: How the stroke composites.

tools.example:
1. Ctrl+A to select the whole canvas.
2. Edit > Stroke..., Width 12 px, white, Location = Inside.
3. Ctrl+D.
tools.notes: For a stroke that must stay editable and scale with the artwork, use Layer > Layer Style > Stroke instead.

tools.name: Edit > Content-Aware Scale
tools.description: Rescales an image while protecting important content: low-detail areas are stretched or squeezed and detailed regions keep their proportions. An alpha channel can be supplied to mark what must not distort, and the Protect Skin Tones button shields people automatically. Used to change an image's aspect ratio without cropping.
tools.usage: Edit > Content-Aware Scale (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+C). Drag the handles and press Enter.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: 0-100% blend between content-aware scaling and a plain scale.

parameters.name: Protect
parameters.description: An alpha channel marking regions to preserve.

parameters.name: Protect Skin Tones
parameters.description: Toolbar toggle that shields people from distortion.

tools.example:
1. Unlock the Background layer.
2. Select the subject and Select > Save Selection as "protect".
3. Alt+Shift+Ctrl+C, set Protect = protect, Amount 100%.
4. Drag the left handle inwards to narrow the frame; press Enter.

tools.name: Edit > Puppet Warp
tools.description: Lays a triangular mesh over the layer and lets you pin points and drag them, deforming the artwork as if it were a puppet. Used to reposition a limb, straighten a bent object, adjust hair or subtly reshape a product. Pin depth controls which part overlaps which where the mesh folds.
tools.usage: Edit > Puppet Warp, with a layer or smart object selected. Click to place pins, drag to move them, press Enter to commit.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Rigid, Normal or Distort - how elastic the mesh is.

parameters.name: Density
parameters.description: Fewer Points, Normal or More Points - mesh resolution against performance.

parameters.name: Expansion
parameters.description: Grows or shrinks the mesh beyond the layer's edges.

parameters.name: Pin Depth / Rotate
parameters.description: Push a pin behind or in front of another; rotate around a selected pin (Auto or a fixed angle).

tools.example:
1. Convert the layer to a smart object so the warp stays editable.
2. Edit > Puppet Warp, Mode = Normal, Density = Normal.
3. Pin the shoulder, elbow and body to hold them still, then drag a pin on the hand to raise the arm.
4. Press Enter.

tools.name: Edit > Perspective Warp
tools.description: Draws quads over the planes of a photographed object, then lets you manipulate the perspective of each plane independently. Used to change the apparent camera angle on a building or box, to straighten converging verticals, and to make a composited element match the perspective of its new scene.
tools.usage: Edit > Perspective Warp. Draw quads in Layout mode, click Warp in the options bar, then drag corners. Enter commits.

parameters.name: Layout / Warp
parameters.description: Two modes: define the planes, then deform them.

parameters.name: Automatic straighten buttons
parameters.description: Straighten near-horizontal lines, near-vertical lines, or both.

tools.example:
1. Convert to a smart object.
2. Edit > Perspective Warp; drag a quad over the front face of the building and a second over the side face, snapping their shared edge.
3. Click Warp, then click the "straighten vertically" button.
4. Press Enter.
tools.notes: Requires the graphics processor. The quads must share edges for the planes to hinge correctly.

tools.name: Edit > Free Transform and the Transform submenu
tools.description: The general-purpose transform: scale, rotate, skew, distort, apply perspective, warp and flip the selected layers, selection contents or path. Since Photoshop 2019 scaling is proportional by default and Shift scales freely; the options bar exposes numeric X, Y, W, H, angle and skew fields plus the reference-point grid.
tools.usage: Edit > Free Transform (Ctrl+T). Then right-click inside the box, or use Edit > Transform > Scale / Rotate / Skew / Distort / Perspective / Warp / Rotate 180 / Rotate 90 CW / Rotate 90 CCW / Flip Horizontal / Flip Vertical. Enter commits, Esc cancels.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Drag a handle; hold Shift for free (non-proportional) scaling and Alt to scale about the centre.

parameters.name: Rotate
parameters.description: Drag outside the box; hold Shift to snap to 15 degree increments.

parameters.name: Skew
parameters.description: Ctrl+Shift+drag an edge handle - slants along one axis.

parameters.name: Distort
parameters.description: Ctrl+drag a corner handle - moves it freely.

parameters.name: Perspective
parameters.description: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+drag a corner - moves the opposite corner symmetrically for a keystone effect.

parameters.name: Warp
parameters.description: A grid with bezier handles, custom grid divisions and preset warps (Arc, Flag, Bulge, ...).

parameters.name: Interpolation / Reference point
parameters.description: Resampling method for the transform, and the anchor the transform pivots around.

tools.example:
1. Ctrl+T.
2. Drag a corner to scale proportionally; hold Alt to scale about the centre.
3. Right-click > Warp, choose Arc from the Warp preset menu, Bend 30%.
4. Press Enter.

JSX:
app.activeDocument.activeLayer.resize(80, 80, AnchorPosition.MIDDLECENTER);
app.activeDocument.activeLayer.rotate(15, AnchorPosition.MIDDLECENTER);
tools.notes: Transform a smart object rather than a pixel layer so repeated transforms never compound resampling loss. Shift+Ctrl+T repeats the last transform.

tools.name: Define Brush Preset, Define Pattern and Define Custom Shape
tools.description: Turns the current selection (or the whole layer) into a reusable preset. Define Brush Preset makes a greyscale brush tip, Define Pattern makes a tile available to fills, the Pattern Stamp and Pattern Overlay, and Define Custom Shape turns the selected path into a vector preset in the Shapes panel.
tools.usage: Edit > Define Brush Preset... / Define Pattern... / Define Custom Shape... (the last requires an active path).

parameters.name: Brush preset
parameters.description: Built from luminance: black is full opacity, white is transparent. Maximum tip size 5000 px.

parameters.name: Pattern
parameters.description: Requires a rectangular selection with Feather = 0, or no selection at all.

parameters.name: Custom shape
parameters.description: Requires a path selected in the Paths panel.

tools.example:
1. Paint a signature in black on a white background.
2. Rectangular Marquee around it, Edit > Define Brush Preset..., name it "signature".
3. Press B, pick the new tip, set the foreground colour and stamp it on any image.
tools.notes: Presets are stored in the current preset set; export them with the panel menu (Export Selected Presets) as .abr, .pat or .csh to share.

tools.name: Edit > Purge
tools.description: Frees the memory held by Undo, the Clipboard, Histories, the Video Cache or All. Used when Photoshop reports it is out of RAM or scratch disk during a long session or a big batch, and inside scripts that process hundreds of files. Purging is not undoable.
tools.usage: Edit > Purge > Undo / Clipboard / Histories / Video Cache / All.
tools.notes: Purging Histories discards every undo state in every open document, so save first.

tools.name: Edit > Color Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts, Menus and Preferences
tools.description: The application-level configuration. Color Settings chooses working spaces (sRGB, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto, the CMYK profile) and the policies applied when a file's profile differs; Keyboard Shortcuts remaps any menu item, tool or panel command and saves the result as a set; Menus hides or colour-codes menu items; Preferences holds General, Interface, Workspace, Tools, History Log, File Handling, Export, Performance (RAM, scratch disks, GPU, history states), Scratch Disks, Cursors, Transparency & Gamut, Units & Rulers, Guides/Grid/Slices, Plug-ins and Type.
tools.usage: Edit > Color Settings... (Shift+Ctrl+K), Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts... (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+K), Edit > Menus... (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+M), Edit > Preferences > General... (Ctrl+K) and the other Preferences panes.

parameters.name: Working Spaces
parameters.description: RGB, CMYK, Gray and Spot profiles used for untagged documents and new files.

parameters.name: Color Management Policies
parameters.description: Preserve Embedded Profiles, Convert to Working, or Off - with the Ask When Opening/Pasting warnings.

parameters.name: Performance
parameters.description: Memory Usage percentage, History States, Cache Levels and Tile Size, and Use Graphics Processor.

parameters.name: Scratch Disks
parameters.description: Which drives Photoshop uses as virtual memory - put the first one on a fast SSD that is not the system disk.

parameters.name: History Log
parameters.description: Records every edit to the file metadata, a text file, or both - useful for audit trails and billing.

tools.example:
1. Shift+Ctrl+K, choose "North America Prepress 2" (or your region's prepress preset) so Adobe RGB is the RGB working space and profiles are preserved.
2. Ctrl+K > Performance: memory 70%, History States 30, Use Graphics Processor ticked.
3. Alt+Shift+Ctrl+K to assign F6 to Filter > Camera Raw Filter, then Save as a named shortcut set.

tools.name: Character and Paragraph panels
tools.description: Full typographic control over type layers. The Character panel holds font family and style, size, leading, kerning, tracking, vertical and horizontal scale, baseline shift, colour, all-caps/small-caps/superscript/subscript/underline/strikethrough, language and anti-aliasing. The Paragraph panel holds alignment and justification, indents, space before and after, hyphenation and the composer. Character Styles and Paragraph Styles panels save these settings as named, reusable styles.
tools.usage: Window > Character, Window > Paragraph, Window > Character Styles, Window > Paragraph Styles. Many settings also appear in the Type tool's options bar.

parameters.name: Leading
parameters.description: Line spacing; Auto is 120% of the type size.

parameters.name: Kerning / Tracking
parameters.description: Space between a specific pair (Metrics, Optical, or a value) and across a run of characters.

parameters.name: Baseline Shift
parameters.description: Raises or lowers characters relative to the baseline.

parameters.name: Hyphenation / Composer
parameters.description: Adobe Every-line Composer gives the most even paragraph rag; Single-line Composer gives predictable per-line behaviour.

parameters.name: Anti-aliasing
parameters.description: None, Sharp, Crisp, Strong, Smooth - and the macOS/Windows LCD variants.

tools.example:
1. Select a type layer and open Window > Character.
2. Set size 42 pt, leading 48 pt, tracking -20, kerning Optical.
3. Click the New Character Style button so the settings can be applied to other layers in one click.
tools.notes: Type layer properties are also scriptable through the TextItem object (size, leading, tracking, justification, font).

tools.name: Type conversion commands (Warp Text, Convert to Shape, Create Work Path, Rasterize Type)
tools.description: Four ways of turning editable type into something else. Warp Text bends the whole layer along a preset curve while keeping the text editable; Convert to Shape turns the characters into a vector shape layer (editable outlines, no longer editable text); Create Work Path produces a path from the letterforms without changing the layer; Rasterize Type turns them into pixels.
tools.usage: Type > Warp Text... (also the warp button in the Type tool's options bar), Type > Convert to Shape, Type > Create Work Path, Type > Rasterize Type Layer (or Layer > Rasterize > Type).

parameters.name: Warp Style
parameters.description: Arc, Arc Lower, Arc Upper, Arch, Bulge, Shell Lower, Shell Upper, Flag, Wave, Fish, Rise, Fisheye, Inflate, Squeeze, Twist.

parameters.name: Bend / Horizontal Distortion / Vertical Distortion
parameters.description: -100% to +100% each, with Horizontal or Vertical orientation.

tools.example:
1. Select the type layer and click the warp button in the options bar.
2. Style = Arc, Bend +30%, OK - the text is curved but still editable.
3. When the design is final, Type > Convert to Shape so the outlines can be edited with the Direct Selection tool and the file no longer depends on the font.

JSX: app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.convertToShape();
tools.notes: Convert to Shape and Rasterize are one-way. Duplicate the type layer and hide the original before converting so the text remains editable.

tools.name: Match Font, variable fonts and the Glyphs panel
tools.description: Three type utilities. Match Font analyses a selected rectangle containing text in an image and suggests matching fonts from those installed and from Adobe Fonts. Variable fonts expose weight, width and slant as continuous sliders in the Properties or Character panel. The Glyphs panel shows every character in a font, including alternates, ligatures, ornaments and swashes, and inserts them into the type layer.
tools.usage: Type > Match Font... (with a rectangular selection around the text in a photo), Window > Glyphs, and the variable-font sliders in Window > Properties when a variable font is selected.

parameters.name: Match Font
parameters.description: Works best on a level, front-on, single-line sample; tick "Show Fonts Available to Activate from Adobe Fonts" to include cloud fonts.

parameters.name: Glyphs panel
parameters.description: Filter by category (Alternates for Selection, Ligatures, Ornaments, Swash, Titling, Fractions, Stylistic Sets) and browse recently used glyphs.

parameters.name: Variable font axes
parameters.description: Weight, Width, Slant and font-specific optical size axes, adjustable continuously.

tools.example:
1. Rectangular Marquee around the headline in a photographed poster.
2. Type > Match Font... and pick the closest suggestion.
3. Set the type with that font, then open Window > Glyphs, filter to "Alternates for Selection" and double-click a swash capital to replace the first letter.
tools.notes: Match Font requires the document to be in RGB mode and the sampled text to be roughly horizontal.
